key_insight: MemSkill reframes static, hand-designed memory operations as learnable and evolvable "memory skills", allowing LLM agents to adapt how they extract, consolidate, and prune memory to diverse interactions and long histories.
problem_solved: Fixed, human-designed memory procedures are rigid and inefficient for varied interaction patterns and long conversation histories, causing suboptimal memory use and degraded agent performance.
method: Represent memory procedures as structured, reusable, parametric "skills" that can be invoked by agents for extraction, consolidation, retrieval, and pruning.
Train and evolve the skill repertoire (via learning and evolutionary/meta-learning mechanisms) so skills improve over time and adapt to new interaction patterns.
Integrate learned skills into the agent loop to dynamically manage long histories, reducing redundancy and preserving salient information for downstream tasks.
impact: Provides AI practitioners a scalable, adaptive framework for agent memory management that improves efficiency, reduces memory bloat, and boosts robustness across diverse tasks and long-term interactions.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing agent loop with modular "memory skill" blocks (extract, consolidate, prune) called during interactions
Evolution chart plotting skill fitness/diversity across generations to visualize how skills improve and specialize
Before/after comparison: memory size vs downstream task performance (static rules vs learned skills)
Annotated interaction timeline showing which skills trigger at each turn and how memory contents change
paper_title: MemSkill: Learning and Evolving Memory Skills for Self-Evolving Agents
paper_authors: Haozhen Zhang, Quanyu Long, Jianzhu Bao, Tao Feng, Weizhi Zhang
